analysis: All three give a sound 'you probably don't need Istio for two services' recommendation, so they differ mainly on calibration to the user's expertise and recall of their specific environment. System A is the weakest: it openly has no context, opens with from-scratch explanations of service meshes, sidecars, and mTLS, and offers only generic guidance with no awareness of the user's stack. Systems B and C both demonstrate a real user model — payment-service still in the monolith, an existing auth-service issuing JWTs, gRPC/Kotlin interceptors — and lead with the decision rather than a tutorial. C edges out B by being more concise, leveraging EKS-native specifics (IRSA, intra-cluster encryption) that show deeper grounding in the existing setup, and trimming the mesh-mechanics preamble that B still partially includes. Ranking: C > B > A.
